source.title: Memorization Capacity for Additive Fine-Tuning with Small ReLU Networks
source.authors: Jy-yong Sohn; Dohyun Kwon; Seoyeon An; Kangwook Lee

page_placements.theme: Constructive arbitrary-label capacity has explicit constraints

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary material supplied.
record.tranche_reason: Extends memorization-capacity analysis to additive fine-tuning and reports theoretical fitting capacity and a synthetic-data experiment. Its results bear on fitting arbitrary labels, but use an added side network rather than the unchanged standard training setup in the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper's theorems give existence bounds for fitting arbitrary target values, including the N=K memorization special case. They do not report standard SGD training, test error, or the claim's unchanged-architecture setup. The synthetic experiment reports fine-tuning loss, not test error. Cited results from prior work are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The main results concern representational capacity for additive fine-tuning, rather than whether standard stochastic-gradient training fits random labels or unstructured inputs. The experiment measures a side network's fine-tuning loss as its size changes. Zero-loss pretraining is stated as setup, without a separately reported training result or training procedure establishing a claim version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors introduce Fine-Tuning Capacity, derive upper and lower bounds for shallow additive ReLU side networks, and describe their synthetic experiment as consistent with the theoretical scaling.
record.recipe_differences: Additive fine-tuning with a frozen pretrained network and an added trainable ReLU side network; theoretical existence bounds plus a synthetic fine-tuning experiment, rather than standard end-to-end SGD fitting of random labels.
record.method_sensitivity: Theoretical neuron bounds vary with network depth, N, and K; the synthetic plot varies N and m.

fits_no_version.finding: Exact additive fine-tuning has worst-case neuron requirements linear in N for two-layer ReLU networks and proportional to the square root of N for three-layer networks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Small ReLU side networks have provable capacity to change arbitrary selected targets while preserving outputs on other samples.

fits_no_version.finding: On synthetic Gaussian inputs with random continuous targets, the minimum side-network size reaching fine-tuning MSE at most 0.04 approximately follows square-root scaling in the number of changed targets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Empirical additive fine-tuning capacity approximately follows the theoretical size scaling on this synthetic regression task.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Uncertainty in Artificial Intelligence
record.problems: Synthetic experiment is on generated data and reports a fine-tuning loss figure without numerical condition-level values or uncertainty. It does not report test error or compare against an unchanged standard training setup.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results were reported separately in the supplied text. Cited prior-work results were excluded.

untested.parts: Successful standard stochastic-gradient fitting of completely random labels under unchanged architecture and hyperparameters, with chance test performance.
Training-time comparison with true labels and convergence as label corruption increases.

Measured zero-error training on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian inputs using the same networks. Gaussian inputs occur in the setup, but zero-loss pretraining is not separately evaluated.
Perfect training fit and progressively worsening test performance across corruption fractions.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Training dynamics comparing learning real patterns with memorizing noise.

record.verdict_notes: The absence of optimizer, test-error, and unchanged-architecture evidence warrants no verdict, rather than limits_scope. The theoretical N=K connection establishes representability, not the empirical training claim.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test standard SGD convergence, test error at chance, the same unchanged architecture and hyperparameters, or generalization on true labels.

rows.subject: 2-layer fully-connected ReLU network g
rows.operation_detail: Theorem bounds the minimum neurons needed to fit arbitrary values on N selected samples and zero on the remaining K−N samples.
rows.measure: Existence bound on minimum neurons m⋆ for exact fitting.
rows.note: Theorem gives an existence result, not an SGD training result. The authors state that N=K recovers the memorization-capacity special case.
rows.check: The bound is correctly transcribed, but proves existence of fitting parameters. It does not measure successful stochastic-gradient training. Capacity is a different construct from V1; partial is therefore inappropriate.

rows.subject: 3-layer fully-connected ReLU network g
rows.operation_detail: Theorem bounds the minimum neurons needed to fit arbitrary values on N selected samples and zero on the remaining K−N samples.
rows.measure: Existence bound on minimum neurons m⋆ for exact fitting.
rows.note: This is an existence/capacity result, not evidence of standard SGD training or chance test error.
rows.check: The theorem bounds representational capacity for bounded arbitrary targets. Its N=K special case does not establish that training finds these parameters, so it cannot show a partial V1 effect.

rows.subject: 3-layer ReLU network gθ
rows.stage_stated: fine-tuning side network; f is frozen
rows.operation_detail: Train gθ to fit a synthetic dataset after randomly reassigning N of K labels; report fine-tuning loss by m and N.

conditions.value: yi ∼ Unif[−1, 1]; N labels redefined as yi′ ∼ Unif[−1, 1]

rows.measure: Fine-tuning mean-squared-error loss and minimum m meeting a stated loss threshold.
rows.value: The text states that the yellow line shows the minimum m satisfying ℓFT(m, N) ≤ 0.04; its plotted values are figure only.
rows.note: Added side network is trained while pretrained f is frozen. The figure's per-condition values are not supplied numerically in the text; no test error is reported.
rows.check: This is a size-dependent additive fine-tuning experiment with a frozen pretrained network. The threshold MSE of 0.04 does not establish zero or near-zero training error for the claim's standard networks. The threshold curve summarizes the method's performance; it is not a condition-level random-label fitting result.

relation.reason: The study discusses memorization capacity and extends it to additive fine-tuning, without testing or using the listed empirical findings.

tranche.reason: Theoretical representational capacity and side-network size versus fine-tuning MSE do not test any listed claim version; stochastic-gradient fitting under unchanged architecture and hyperparameters is not established.
